newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Intracom sees 25 pct profit growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Greek Intracom sees 25 pct profit growth in 97.

text.p: Greece's high-tech telecoms manufacturer Intracom sees earnings growth of 25 percent in 1997, its chairman Socrates Kokkalis told shareholders on Monday.
Intracom's pretax profit was forecast to reach 9.0 billion drachmas on turnover growth of 20.6 percent to 55.0 billion this year, said Kokkalis.
Turnover was seen growing another 36 percent to over 75.0 billion drachmas in 1998.
These were conservative estimates as they excluded the likely impact of additional sales for the 1997-98 Fast Track investment programme of OTE telecom, budgeted at 135 billion drachmas, he said.
Intracom posted pretax profit of 7.202 billion drachmas on turnover of 45.61 billion in 1996.

Management said it will seek approval at an extraordinary meeting schedule for September 1997 for a 20 billion drachma rights issue in which Salomon Brothers will act as global coordinator and lead underwriter.
Intracom will pay a dividend per share of 200 drachmas for fiscal 1996 versus 163.3 in the previous year.
Its shares start trading ex-dividend July 1.
